newsitem.title: UK: Cuba returns as main origin in sugar freight order.
newsitem.headline: Cuba returns as main origin in sugar freight order.

text.p: London's sugar freight market stayed busy at the end of the week as Cuba resumed its role as centre of interest after Cargill's spate of enquiry from south Brazil, shipbrokers said on Friday.
Shipbrokers said no more activity had been sighted from U.S. trade house Cargill, which is attempting to place hefty amounts of raw sugar delivered against the New York raws May futures expiry.

Pacol quoted for 14,500 tonnes of bulk sugar on its usual run from Cuba to the Black Sea for prompt/onwards dates, while E D & F Man was open for 25,000 tonnes from the Philippines to US Gulf/Atlantic for end-May.
Shipbrokers said Vitol was in the market for 23/25,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Maceio to the Black Sea for the first half of May.

They cited market talk that Lorico fixed 16,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Cuba to Alexandria for the end of May and Benham fixed 14/18,000 tonnes in bags from Puerto Quetzal to Toronto for the second half of May.
Details of rates have yet to emerge.
